name: Artisan
tagline: Ava, the AI BDR, an autonomous sales agent that sources leads, runs multi-channel outbound and books meetings without a human writing each message.
verdict: Artisan's Ava is one of the more complete "AI BDR" plays on the market: since the May 2026 Ava 2.0 rebuild she runs the full outbound motion autonomously, sourcing, enrichment, multi-channel outreach, reply and objection handling, and meeting booking, with a native dialer bridging the loop to a human for calls. The company is well-capitalised (~$37M+ raised, led by Glade Brook Capital with HubSpot Ventures and Y Combinator) and backs its pitch with specific, published customer numbers rather than vague praise. But two things temper the recommendation: pricing is entirely opaque (every tier is "Talk to sales," and the self-serve entry tier the company announced at launch isn't visible on the live site), and Artisan has racked up a genuine string of controversies in a short window, a viral "Stop Hiring Humans" campaign, a three-week LinkedIn ban over a data vendor's ToS violation, and a publicized (since-settled) dispute over unauthorised use of a cartoonist's artwork. Pick Artisan if you're a funded sales team ready to run a proper paid pilot and judge Ava on your own reply and booking data; look elsewhere if you need transparent self-serve pricing or want to avoid a vendor whose brand has drawn this much recent scrutiny.
